title: Balanced module open projection and normalized underived unit
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion, and $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On small representatives of the pro-étale sites in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for $T=U,Z$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ for internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with relative tensor $\otimes_{\Lambda_T}$ [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Let $E=j_!:\mathcal M_U\to\mathcal M_Z$ be the coefficient-linear extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and $R=j^*:\mathcal M_Z\to\mathcal M_U$ the module pullback [def-sfb-module-upper-star], with their specified adjunction $E\dashv R$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], unit $u$ and counit $v$. Use the actual relative tensor comparison $\nu_{A,B}:RA\otimes_{\Lambda_U}RB\to R(A\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}B)$ of module pullback, induced by its abelian pullback structure and scalar extension along $\alpha_j$: it is the inverse of the ordinary comparison $t_{A,B}$ of [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison] for $f=j$, under that node's identification of its inverse image with $R$.
Both $E$ and $R$ are additive and exact. The unit $u_M:M\to REM$ is invertible for every $M\in\mathcal M_U$; after the coefficient identification $\alpha_j$, its underlying map is the abelian extension-by-zero adjunction unit, and the inverse underlying map is $\Lambda_U$-linear.
For every $M\in\mathcal M_U$, $N\in\mathcal M_Z$, the map
$$\theta_{M,N}=v_{EM\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}N}\circ E(\nu_{EM,N})\circ E(u_M\otimes1_{RN}):E(M\otimes_{\Lambda_U}RN)\longrightarrow EM\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}N$$
is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_Z$-modules, natural in both variables. Its transpose is exactly $\nu_{EM,N}\circ(u_M\otimes1)$ for the specified module adjunction. Under the canonical abelian projection isomorphisms for $M,N$ and for the additional coefficient factor, the two arrows of the balanced coequalizer defining the source relative tensor identify, respectively, with the two arrows defining the target relative tensor, using $\alpha_j:j^{-1}\Lambda_Z\cong\Lambda_U$. The induced map on their coequalizers is $\theta_{M,N}$. Here the balanced coequalizers and actions are those of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]; the tensors before taking these coequalizers are abelian-sheaf tensors. No derived or constructibility assertion is included.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: the identity viewed through j^*j_!=id and its adjoint theta; returned proof Steps 1-2, coefficient-linear unit and balanced relative-tensor normalization

proof.text: Put $P=j^{\Ab}_!$, $S=j^*_{\Ab}$, $B=\Lambda_Z$ and $B'=SB$. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_j:B'\to\Lambda_U$ is invertible. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](5), extension and coextension along $\alpha_j$ are the same canonical transport as restriction along $\alpha_j^{-1}$. Thus we may calculate with $B'$-modules, restoring $\alpha_j$ at the end. The given functors become the linearization of $P$ and transport along $S$. The adjunction of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] is, under these identifications, the restricted abelian Hom bijection: [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-transport-adjunction] says explicitly that a linear map corresponds to its abelian adjunct. In particular its unit and counit forget to those of $P\dashv S$. The scalar identification here sends a scalar tensor $b\otimes m$ to $\alpha_j(b)m$, so uses the canonical scalar adjunction, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of right adjoints.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: normalize the specified module adjunction

proof.text: The functor $E$ is additive and exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. To check this for $R$, use its formula [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and the invertible scalar transport of Step 1: its underlying functor is $S$. The functor $S$ is additive and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], applied to the pro-étale site morphism on the chosen small representatives. Abelian sheaves form abelian categories by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]; their tensor is additive and preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Hence the hypotheses of [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] hold for $S$ and its module lift. It gives additivity and exactness of $R$ with the scalar transport restored.

source.place: Opening paragraph: exactness of the open operations

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek], $P$ is fully faithful. Here is directly why its unit $\eta_M$ is invertible. Fullness gives $e:SPM\to M$ with $Pe=\varepsilon_{PM}$. The first triangle and faithfulness give $e\eta_M=1$. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $\eta_M e=SP(e)\eta_{SPM}=S(\varepsilon_{PM})\eta_{SPM}=1$ by the other triangle. By Step 1 the module unit $u_M$ has this underlying map. Its inverse is linear: from $u\gamma_M=\gamma_{REM}(\Lambda_U\otimes u)$, compose on the left by $u^{-1}$ and on the right by $\Lambda_U\otimes u^{-1}$ to obtain $u^{-1}\gamma_{REM}=\gamma_M(\Lambda_U\otimes u^{-1})$. Thus it is a module isomorphism with exactly the required underlying normalization.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: the specified unit realizes j^*j_!=id

proof.text: For the remainder calculate after Step 1's coefficient identification. Suppress underlying-sheaf notation and associators. Let $\beta_{M,L}:P(M\otimes SL)\xrightarrow{\sim}PM\otimes L$ be the abelian projection isomorphism, with factors reversed by the symmetric braiding from the order in [lem-sfb-open-projection-formula]. The inverse image respects these symmetries by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided]. Its abelian transpose is $\mu_{PM,L}(\eta_M\otimes1)$, where $\mu$ is the strong monoidal structure of $S$. By [def-sfb-adjunction-projection-formula] these projection maps satisfy the unit and associativity equations of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. The $B$-action on $EM=PM$ is exactly $P\gamma_M$ after the inverse projection isomorphism with coefficient factor $B$, by [def-sfb-module-linear-open-lower-shriek]. These facts supply both the actual maps and their coherence for an additional coefficient factor; objectwise isomorphisms alone would not suffice.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: abelian projection isomorphism with its coefficient-factor coherence

proof.text: Write $a=\gamma_M\sigma_{M,B'}$ for the right $B'$-action on $M$, with $\sigma$ denoting the symmetric braiding, and $b=\gamma_N$ for the left $B$-action on $N$. By [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor], the source balancing arrows before $P$ are $d_1=a\otimes1$ and $d_2=1\otimes(Sb\circ\mu_{B,N})$, from $M\otimes B'\otimes SN$ to $M\otimes SN$. The target arrows are $e_1=a_{EM}\otimes1$ and $e_2=1\otimes b$ from $EM\otimes B\otimes N$ to $EM\otimes N$. Put $H_0=\beta_{M,N}$ and $H_1=\beta_{M,B\otimes N}\circ P(1\otimes\mu_{B,N})$. Then $H_0P(d_2)=e_2H_1$ by naturality of $\beta$ in $N$. Also $H_0P(d_1)=e_1H_1$: substitute $a_{EM}=P(a)\beta_{M,B}^{-1}$ (the symmetric form of the action in Step 4), and the resulting equality is exactly the associativity equation for the projection formula in [def-sfb-projection-formula], with factors permuted by the symmetric braiding. Thus each arrow, in its original order, corresponds to the correct target arrow. Restoring coefficients replaces the $B'$-actions by their composites with $\alpha_j$ and changes neither equation.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: the two balanced-coequalizer arrows

proof.text: Since $P$ is left adjoint to $S$ by [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek], it preserves the balancing coequalizer by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; its indexing category is the finite parallel-pair category in the fixed universe. Thus Step 5's isomorphism of parallel-pair diagrams induces an isomorphism $h:P(M\otimes_{B'}RN)\to PM\otimes_BN$. Explicitly, if $q_U,q_Z$ denote the two balanced quotient projections, $hP(q_U)=q_ZH_0$; the inverse is induced by $H_0^{-1},H_1^{-1}$, and their composites are identities by the coequalizer uniqueness property. The quotient actions are the actions through the first factor of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. The map $h$ is $B$-linear: precompose its required action equation with $B\otimes P(q_U)$ and use Step 4's coefficient-factor projection comparison. The equation reduces to the defining action on $PM$, since $q_Z$ is linear. This precomposition detects equality because $B\otimes-$ preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The same argument, or multiplying this equation by the inverse of $h$, makes $h^{-1}$ linear.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: induce the module isomorphism on balanced quotients

proof.text: It remains to identify the map, rather than only its invertibility. Let $w=\nu_{EM,N}(u_M\otimes1)$ in the module category. By the balanced-generator normalization in [def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison], its underlying map satisfies $wq_U=S(q_Z)\mu_{PM,N}(\eta_M\otimes1)$. On the other hand the abelian transpose $S(h)\eta_{M\otimes_{B'}RN}$, precomposed with $q_U$, equals $S(hP(q_U))\eta_{M\otimes SN}=S(q_ZH_0)\eta_{M\otimes SN}=S(q_Z)\mu_{PM,N}(\eta_M\otimes1)$, by naturality of the unit and the transpose characterization of $H_0$. The quotient projection $q_U$ is epic by its coequalizer property, so the transposes agree. Step 1 identifies this with equality of module transposes. The inverse Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] therefore gives $h=v_{EM\otimes_BN}\circ E(w)=\theta_{M,N}$. This proves both the displayed formula and its exact transpose with the specified comparison $\nu=t^{-1}$.

source.place: Open immersions, sheaves: theta is the adjoint of the normalized tensor-unit map

proof.text: All the equations above are natural in $M$ and $N$: $H_0$ and $H_1$ are natural projection comparisons, the balanced projections are functorial, and the Hom bijection is natural. For maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, the naturality square for $h$ commutes after precomposition with $P(q_U)$ by the defining equation $hP(q_U)=q_ZH_0$ and naturality of $H_0$; this projection is epic, so the square commutes. Hence the isomorphisms are natural module isomorphisms. The construction uses only ordinary abelian tensors and their balanced coequalizers; no derived category or constructibility statement has entered.
